claims.supporting_quote: Recent research published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences showed that some microbes living in Antarctic soils appear to exist nowhere else on Earth.

claims.claim: University of Reading researchers loaded nitric oxide into organosilica nanoparticles that release the gas slowly over hours.
claims.episode_span: University of Reading researchers loaded nitric oxide into organosilica nanoparticles that release the gas slowly over hours.
claims.source_title: Gas inside us could fight wound infections, moth study shows
claims.supporting_quote: A new study led by scientists at the University of Reading found that tiny particles releasing nitric oxide helped nine in 10 infected wax moth larvae survive bacterial infections, compared with around six in 10 that were not treated.

claims.claim: Researchers examined long-term records from La Selva in Costa Rica and El Verde in Puerto Rico, finding days exceeding the 95th-percentile heat threshold rose from eight per year to thirty at La Selva by 2024.
claims.episode_span: Average temperatures changed little, yet days exceeding the 95th-percentile heat threshold rose from eight per year to thirty at La Selva by 2024.
claims.source_title: Climate change is making the tropics hotter
claims.supporting_quote: In La Selva prior to 2024, you had an average of eight hot days—days where the temperature exceeded the 95th percentile of temperatures at that site—per year. Now that number is up to 30.

claims.claim: Cambridge University scientists analyzed seventy years of sea-level records around northwestern Europe and used machine learning to group coastlines that experience extreme surge events together.
claims.episode_span: Cambridge University scientists analyzed seventy years of sea-level records around northwestern Europe. They isolated extreme surge events and used machine learning to group coastlines that experience them together.
claims.source_title: UK storm surges have far-flung, global climate connections
claims.supporting_quote: Studying 70 years of sea level data, the researchers found that global atmospheric conditions thousands of kilometers distant can determine which coastlines bear the brunt of extreme storm surges around the North Sea, English Channel and Irish Sea.
